title: Which Compute, Which Data?
subtitle: Polar Switch · Loop depth · Tabular data scaling · Score-SDE
intro: Three main readings: polar-decomposition circuits, forward/backward compute budgets, and distribution shift under data scaling. Another 31 new-preprint/technical-blog briefs and 25 unverified revision notices retain their original dates. The Score-SDE classic derives the one-half factor in probability flow.

articles.paper: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
articles.authors: Zhehang Du · Weijie Su
articles.title: Polar Switch: optimize the circuit before approximating polar
articles.evidence: Read Sections 3–4 and experimental tables; not independently reproduced

blocks.text: Muon's cost depends on reusing matrix products, not only polynomial degree. For normalized X, Polar Switch searches polynomial circuits with limited buffers; the corresponding singular-value map is an odd polynomial. [1]

blocks.tex: X=U\Sigma V^\top,\qquad X\leftarrow h(XX^\top)X=U[\Sigma h(\Sigma^2)]V^\top,\qquad p(\sigma)=\sigma h(\sigma^2)
blocks.label: Spectral map in exact arithmetic; not an elementwise rule for arbitrary noncommuting buffers
Restricted circuit: k matrix products; both coefficients and buffer connections are searched

rows: Polar Express
blocks.caption: n×m, n≤m, α=m/n; input singular values [0.001,1], exact arithmetic. PS2/3 use 2/3 buffers. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Square-matrix kernel time falls 15.5–18.7% versus Polar Express, not end-to-end training time. Long Qwen-0.6B / Gemma-1B runs use one seed each; the rounding model omits some additive errors. [1]

articles.paper: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
articles.authors: Xuyuan Xiong · Siyu Chen · Zihan Shao · Yue Su · Weiyang Jin · Ping Luo · Zhuoran Yang · Xihui Liu
articles.title: Loop depth versus backward depth: truncation need not save compute
articles.evidence: Read setup, fitted law, budget analysis and validation experiments

blocks.text: Let T be forward loops and B≤T backward loops. Across 592 runs with 58–919M non-embedding parameters, repeated computation is mapped to effective parameters; N_once / N_rec count non-recurrent / recurrent parameters. [2]

blocks.label: Empirical fit; D counts training tokens, not a universal scaling theorem
Fitted p=0.23677, q=1.02181; C approximates leading FLOPs
Within the feasible continuous relaxation: when T and B are both free, the fitted model favors full backpropagation

blocks.caption: FineWeb-Edu, matched theoretical FLOPs; matrix parameters use MuonH. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Fixing T differs from optimizing both T and B. If parameter count is also free, this fit favors non-looped models within the studied budget range. Results depend on bounded g, architecture and training range. [2]

articles.paper: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
articles.authors: Ivan Rubachev · Nikita Lazarev · Artem Babenko
articles.title: More data makes the validation distribution matter
articles.evidence: Read Sections 3–5 and fitting details in the appendix

blocks.text: Eight real tabular tasks scale to ten million samples, evaluated under random splits and temporal/group shifts. Error separates into a decreasing term and a floor for dataset d and method m: [3]

blocks.label: E is RMSE or 1−AP; shared exponents are shared within a dataset only

rows: Cooking
Jane Street
blocks.caption: 71 curves, 9 methods; mean R² drops by less than 0.01 on 7/8 tasks when sharing exponents. These are in-sample fits. [3]

blocks.text: Tuning on in-distribution validation can worsen out-of-distribution performance as data grows. Deployment-representative validation mitigates this in MLP experiments; adding OOD examples to PFN context does not always fix it. [3]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: High fitted R² does not establish reliable extrapolation, nor a universal exponent across tasks. The study does not prove that more data necessarily harms generalization.

articles.paper: T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training
articles.authors: Dongyang Li · Mingsong Yan · Zheng Zhang · Sui Tang
articles.title: T-MUON: tensorized spectral updates
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Extends Muon using t-SVD and transform-domain operators. Preferred tensorizations vary across 51M–1.3B pretraining models; one transform's advantage is not universal. [4]

articles.paper: A Statistical Viewpoint on Adam, Shampoo and Muon
articles.authors: Tetiana Parshakova · Robert M. Gower · Paulo Orenstein
articles.title: A statistical model of Muon
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Connects Adam, Shampoo and Muon through structured gradient covariance, proposing MN-Muon. It beats Muon in small GPT comparisons, but is comparable to or slightly below NorMuon in the best medium-scale configurations. [5]

articles.paper: How Does Muon Work in Private Deep Learning? Scalable Differentially Private Training via Orthogonalization
articles.authors: Alexander Gaponov · Grigory Malinovsky · Egor Shulgin · Peter Richtarik
articles.title: DP-Muon: clipping matters alongside privacy noise
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Analyzes clipping alongside orthogonalization; the best optimizer in language-model experiments still depends on batch size. The abstract does not support an unconditional rate or uniform superiority to DP-Adam. [6]

articles.paper: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
articles.authors: Keshigeyan Chandrasegaran · Yue Zhao · Armin W. Thomas · Ehsan Adeli · Jiajun Wu · Juan Carlos Niebles · Li Fei-Fei · Michael Poli
articles.title: Halcyon: does text-to-image need language pretraining?
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Trains from scratch on 100M image–text pairs. Controlled experiments find no T2I gain from text-only pretraining. Cross-model compute ratios compare different training recipes, not strictly matched single-model ablations. [7]

articles.title: Ropedia W0: human experience and robot data
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Uses about 10k hours of human video and 3k hours of robot experience for a cross-embodiment world model, reporting benefits from both data axes; no power-law exponent is verified here. [8]

articles.paper: Where is Physical RSI capability from? An Observational Scaling Law of LLM-as-policy
articles.authors: Zekai Li · Jiayi Yu · Jinlu Zhang · Luyang Niu · Zekun Qi · Jun Zheng · Xuchuan Chen · Dairu Liu · Yintianrun Zhang · He Wang · Li Yi
articles.title: Physical RSI: observational capability forecasting
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Across 18 manipulation tasks with fixed interaction budgets, capability proxies and early feedback forecast self-improvement. Observational relationships do not identify causal effects of individual scaling axes. [9]

articles.paper: Answer Delivery Under a Shared Token Budget: An Audited Study of Stopping and Finalization
articles.authors: Yupeng Chang · Linyuan Gao · Zhiyuan Li · Yuan Wu · Yi Chang
articles.title: Answer delivery also costs tokens
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Charges finalization prompts to the shared budget. On 100 fresh GSM8K problems per checkpoint, accuracy rises 8/7 percentage points, while physical token-slot savings remain below 1%. [10]

articles.paper: BOSS: Token-Budgeted Online Sampling and Selection for LLM Reasoning
articles.authors: Yupeng Chang · Yahan Li · Chenlu Guo · Diana Inkpen · Yuan Wu · Yi Chang
articles.title: BOSS: generate, judge and stop under one budget
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Charges both prompt and completion tokens while allocating generation, judging and stopping online. Best in 22 of 24 configurations, within the compared policies and budget grid. [11]

articles.paper: Large-Scale Biomedical RAG: Corpus Scaling, Document Representation, and Efficiency Trade-offs
articles.authors: Adrián Sánchez-Freire · Gonzalo Pérez-Gómez · Aitziber Atutxa · Ander Barrena
articles.title: RAG: corpus growth also grows distractors
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Holds relevant documents fixed while adding distractors to study retrieval rankings and storage/retrieval granularity. This is corpus scaling, not parameter scaling. [12]

articles.authors: Abhinav Khattar · Aishwarya Chhabra · Ameya Velingker · Anusha Kamath · Brandon Norick · Kanishk Singla · Kiran Praveen · Markus Kliegl · Mohammad Qazim Bhat · Mostofa Patwary · Niket Agarwal · Rajpreet Thethy · Ramani Akkati · Raviraj Joshi · Sai Nishanth Padala · Shuoyang Ding · Sriharsha Niverty · Utkarsh Vaidya · Vitaly Lavrukhin · Yev Meyer · Anoop Kunchukuttan · Mitesh Khapra · Mohammed Safi Ur Rahman Khan · Rudra Murthy · Sumanth Doddapaneni · Thanmay Jayakumar · Ujjwal Sharma
articles.title: Indic: mixing synthetic pretraining data
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Builds a 2.83T-token resource across 22 languages and studies synthetic/natural text and English mixtures in continued pretraining. Mixture gains remain language- and evaluation-dependent. [13]

articles.paper: Keep the Lineages Alive: Diversity-Preserving SMC for Diffusion LLM Decoding
articles.authors: Minoo Ahmadi · Seyedarmin Azizi · Mehdi Kamal · Massoud Pedram
articles.title: LP-SMC: particle count is not lineage diversity
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Uses Chopthin and retention to reduce lineage collapse in diffusion-language decoding. Oracle coverage improves, with final accuracy improving in 11/12 cases. Reset ESS alone does not establish restored diversity. [14]

articles.paper: Adaptive Decoding Methods for Token-Efficient Reinforcement Learning
articles.authors: Zhaonan Li · Zelei Cheng · Amritansh Mishra · Chia-Hsuan Lee · Mann Patel · Sambit Sahu · Ben Zhou · William M. Campbell
articles.title: RLVR: limits of adaptive decoding support
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Expands top-k for a 4B code model under 150M tokens. It beats fixed k=10 but is close to the best fixed k=20; the single test run ties. This does not establish universal superiority to fixed policies. [15]

articles.authors: Zhongyin Wang · Zhaoqian Xue · Junting Mu · Haozheng Liu · Ye Yuan · Haolun Wu · Lingyao Li
articles.title: Decision models after truncated reasoning
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Evaluates 35 model pairings with a small decision model reading truncated traces. Cost benefits are offline held-out estimates, not direct measurements of online deployment savings. [16]

articles.paper: Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere
articles.authors: Arber Zela · Artavazd Maranjyan · Pol Puigdemont · David Berghaus · Valentyn Boreiko · Volkan Cevher
articles.title: Spherical fixed-point reasoning and adaptive halting
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Constrains recurrent states to a sphere and chooses depth through fixed-point residuals. The abstract describes conditional stability; without full assumptions, it is not reported as unconditional convergence. [17]

articles.paper: Curriculum Learning Teaches LLMs Long-Horizon Implicit Reasoning, Up To A Limit
articles.authors: Jimson Huang · Maxwell Nickell · Ruowang Zhang · Abulhair Saparov
articles.title: A horizon ceiling for curriculum learning
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: At matched compute, curriculum learning improves implicit long-horizon reasoning, but look-ahead saturates; scaling training does not remove the observed task-specific ceiling. [18]

articles.paper: ATEST: Adaptive Resource-Aware Test-Time Scaling for LLM Inference
articles.authors: Mobina Kashaniyan · Ali Jannesari
articles.title: ATEST: budgets respond to system load
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Includes GPU load and energy in inference-budget control, trading accuracy against latency and throughput. Equal token budgets need not mean equal system cost. [19]

articles.paper: Test-Time Scaling of Text-to-Image Flow Matching Models with Noise-Rejuvenated Sequential Monte Carlo

articles.title: Noise-rejuvenated SMC for flow matching
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Refreshes latent noise to preserve search diversity for test-time scaling of deterministic flow matching. This is not simply replacing the original ODE with a reverse diffusion SDE. [20]

articles.paper: P(Yes): 15$\times$ Improvements via Test-Time Scaling of Decision Models
articles.authors: Lev Stambler
articles.title: P(Yes): what is the baseline behind 15×?
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Search uses a frozen decision model's yes score; fully solved puzzles rise from 2 to 30 out of 128. The 15× ratio starts from a small baseline and should not replace absolute success rates. [21]

articles.title: ATLAS: concentrate search in selected latents
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Uses attention to target local candidates in visual autoregressive generation under a search budget. Relative gains on targeted categories are not overall image-quality gains. [22]

articles.title: BatchParScale: sparse communication across streams
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Mixes states between parallel streams at selected positions, improving language modeling. Loss gains and factual-retrieval gains do not coincide and should not be conflated. [24]

articles.title: E-process stopping: which error is controlled?
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Uses online signal tests to shorten reasoning. The Ville-type bound controls signal false alarms under the relevant null, not the final-answer error rate. [25]

articles.paper: Revealing what benchmark scores hide: Jointly measuring the breadth and reliability of LLM capabilities using accessibility profiles

articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Data-filtering effects in protein language models vary with model scale, while later fine-tuning can weaken their durability. This brief records only scaling and distributional findings. [29]

articles.title: C-OPSD: not every trajectory needs distillation
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: A signal–noise model fitted at small group size tracks gradient alignment at larger groups. Filtering and packing reduce measured training time by about 40%, while rollout generation is unchanged. [30]

articles.paper: recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models
articles.authors: Saurav Jha · Qianli Liao · Robert Vernon · Sarath Chandar · Quentin Fournier

articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Compares 155M unique parameters trained on 2T tokens with a 350M baseline. Adaptive gating further reduces expected depth, with task-dependent accuracy trade-offs; included for test-time compute scaling. [31]

articles.paper: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models
articles.authors: Agus Sudjianto · Denis Burakov

articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Gaussian surrogates yield finite-sample risks: more student samples need not remove teacher bias, and fixed representations help below a sample-size threshold. The surrogate assumptions are essential. [32]

articles.paper: Are We Evaluating VLM Token Pruning Right? Looking Beyond Accuracy and Token Count

articles.title: Visual token count is not actual compute
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full theorems and experimental tables not checked

blocks.text: Across eight pruning methods, three VLMs and nine benchmarks, equal token counts entail different end-to-end costs; speedup rankings change under a common capability-preservation target. [33]

articles.paper: Nesso 3: A 0.4B model that calls tools in Italian and English
articles.authors: Alessandro Ercolani · Edoardo Federici
articles.title: Nesso 3: failed data mixtures are informative
articles.dateNote: Published 2026-10-19; time of day not stated
articles.evidence: Read training setup, tool-use tables and negative results; not reproduced

blocks.text: The SFT-trained 0.4B model scores 74 on a 100-item tool test. Adding long-chain ToolMind data scores 49; stronger on-policy distillation reaches 75 but hurts Italian instruction-following and academic metrics, so it is excluded from the release. Over-refusal and mixture adjustments are also documented. Small tests, unreleased synthetic data and limited replication constrain generalization. [34]

classic.title: Score-SDE: same marginals, different paths
classic.paper: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
classic.authors: Yang Song · Jascha Sohl-Dickstein · Diederik P. Kingma · Abhishek Kumar · Stefano Ermon · Ben Poole
classic.evidence: Read Sections 3.1–3.4 and 4.3 and checked the equation page; experiments not rerun
classic.question: After replacing the exact score by the same imperfect s_theta, do the reverse SDE and probability-flow ODE still share marginals? Write their density equations and identify the term that no longer cancels.

blocks.text: NCSN (2019) learned scores at multiple noise levels; DDPM (2020) learned discrete denoising chains. Score-SDE unifies them in continuous time: can one score define both stochastic sampling and a deterministic flow? This is historical reading, not news. [60,61]

blocks.label: p_t is the forward marginal density, W Brownian motion; here g is scalar and time-dependent only
Denoising score matching: tractable perturbation kernels supervise the marginal score via conditional scores
Reverse-time SDE; integration runs backward with dt<0, so a forward-time Euler sign convention cannot be copied blindly

blocks.text: The factor of one half comes from conservation of probability, not from simply deleting noise: rewrite Fokker–Planck as a continuity equation. [60]

blocks.label: Short derivation of the paper's probability-flow relation; requires suitable smoothness of densities and coefficients
Probability-flow ODE: exact scores give the same time marginals as the forward SDE, not the same path distribution

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Reverse generation also requires a matching terminal distribution. Score error, terminal approximation and numerical discretization can break the ideal equivalence; deterministic does not mean integration-free.
